newsitem.title: TAIWAN: POLL-Taiwan June industry output seen up 7.94 pct.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Taiwan June industry output seen up 7.94 pct.

text.p: A Reuters Poll on Friday projected an average 7.94 percent year-on-year growth for Taiwan's industrial output in June, reflecting what polled economists called a sound local economic recovery.
The official figures were to be released by the economics ministry at 0230 GMT on July 22.
Industrial output rose 7.34 percent year-on-year in May, and rose an average 6.47 percent year-on-year in January-May.

Economists generally said June's industrial output would be sound as the domestic economic recovery was continuing.

They also attributed the relatively high growth forecast in part to a comparatively low base in June 1996, when the industrial output index stood at 122.03 -- representing a 0.47 percent decline year-on-year at the time.

Economists said they did not expect significant impact from torrential rains that struck Taiwan in June, which had caused total losses of T$1.62 billion, mainly in agriculture, according to government estimates.
"The torrential rains mainly damaged crops, while the impact on industrial output should be limited," said Nomura Securities economist Amy Huang.
Economists said they expected industrial output growth to be higher from July as the electronics and information industry enters its annual hot-sale season.
